title: Verify HAE's percent scale (0-1 vs 0-100) on the first real live push
description:
The live-path mirror of healthie-4u7, which settled the same question for the Apple Health EXPORT path (answer there: 0-1 fractions, x100 conversion added).

Nothing in this repo records what scale HAE sends for percent-typed metrics (body_fat_percentage, blood_oxygen_saturation, walking_asymmetry_percentage, walking_double_support_percentage). healthie-4u7's finding does NOT transfer: Apple's exporter and HAE are different producers, and HealthKit's HKUnit.percent() being a 0-1 fraction internally says nothing about what either tool writes out.

Raised by the plan reviewer on healthie-ei8/55h/c47 (2026-08-01) as a blocking finding: the shared convert_to_canonical multiplies %->% by 100, calibrated against export.xml only. Routing live points through it unchanged would either (a) turn HAE's 30.3 into 3030, blow the (0,100] plausibility bound, and quarantine all four percent kinds on EVERY push forever, or (b) silently fix a real 100x-low live bug. Neither should happen by accident.

RESOLVED IN THE INTERIM by making percent scale a per-INTAKE parameter rather than a property of the unit — the deeper fix, since scale is a property of the PRODUCER. The live path defaults to NO scaling, preserving today's behavior exactly.

ACTION on the first real HAE push (or as soon as Steve checks the app): read the observed span for a percent kind. 0.303 means HAE sends fractions and the live intake needs scale=100; 30.3 means it sends percent and no scaling is correct. Then set the live intake's scale and re-push.

No live data exists yet (backend not deployed, healthie-93n), so nothing stored is at risk today.
acceptance_criteria:
- HAE's percent scale determined from a real payload or the app
- The live intake's scale parameter set accordingly, with the evidence recorded
- A percent-kind live ingest test pins the conclusion
notes:
CLOSE CONDITION — one command, once Steve's phone is back on the LAN (found by hardening-author 2026-08-02; it attempted this read-only and got curl exit 7, connection refused after 1005ms — device off-network, HAE not running, or the IP moved):

curl -sS -X POST http://192.168.10.186:9000/mcp \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $(jq -r '.mcpServers["health-auto-export"].headers.Authorization' .mcp.json | cut -d' ' -f2)" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -H 'Accept: application/json, text/event-stream' \
  -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"get_health_metrics","arguments":{}}}'

Read the raw magnitude for body_fat_percentage / blood_oxygen_saturation. Near 30 and 98 => HAE sends 0-100, no scaling needed (the current default is already correct). Near 0.30 and 0.98 => HAE sends fractions and Producer::HealthAutoExport::percent_scale() must become 100.0. That is a ONE-LINE change in ONE place by design.

SECOND, EASIER CLOSE PATH: the implementation adds a live-path tripwire — ingest_hae warns when a percent-kind value lands in (0.0, 1.0], naming this bead. So the first real push after the odroid deploy (healthie-93n) answers this from the logs without needing the phone reachable at all.

title: Plausibility validation for incoming metric values (both intake paths)
description:
Raised by the final code reviewer on healthie-4lf.1 (2026-07-31).

Neither ingest_hae nor the Apple Health importer applies any range or sign validation to incoming values. A negative StepCount record is summed; an absurd magnitude lands unchallenged in daily_metric. Non-finite values ARE now rejected on the import path (apple_health/parse.rs) and are still unguarded on the live path (see healthie-ei8) — but finite-and-implausible is unguarded on both.

Per CLAUDE.md the project's convention is that validation lives in services, never in handlers or MCP tools, so a per-kind plausibility check belongs in the service layer next to the existing typed-vocabulary enforcement. Per-kind bounds are natural given MetricKind is already a closed vocabulary with a unit() — e.g. Steps >= 0, Spo2 in 0..=100 (or 0..=1 pending healthie-4u7), sleep hours 0..=24.

Decide the posture deliberately: reject the point, clamp, or quarantine it. Quarantine matches ADR-0002's 'never silently dropped' better than rejection.
acceptance_criteria:
- Per-kind plausibility bounds enforced in the service layer on both intake paths
- Implausible values are quarantined or rejected, never silently stored
- Table-driven tests over MetricKind
notes:
CONFIRMED NECESSARY by the first real export import (2026-08-01, 3.2GB / 7.6M records, 15 years). Concrete cases found in Steve's actual data:

1. sleep-total = 49.88 h on 2023-12-29, time-in-bed = 52.95 h. NOT an importer bug — verified against the raw XML: the 'Sleep Cycle' app was left running and wrote AsleepUnspecified 2023-12-29 00:44:39 -> 14:30:12 (13.8h) plus 2023-12-29 15:52:45 -> 2023-12-31 03:59:51 (36.1h), and InBed 2023-12-29 00:24 -> 2023-12-31 03:59:51 (51.6h). The interval union correctly totals what the file says; the file is wrong. Next-highest sleep day is 14.34 h, so this is a lone outlier, not systematic.
2. spo2 minimum = 0.000 across 962 days. A 0% oxygen saturation reading is not survivable; it is a sensor artifact landing in the min column.
3. body-fat and gait-asymmetry minimums also 0.000.

Why this is now P1 rather than P2: healthie-4lf.2's anomaly detection thresholds on daily_metric.max/min. A 49.88h sleep night and a 0.000 spo2 floor will either mask real episodes or manufacture fake ones. M2b trends (healthie-bx9) will also skew.

Suggested bounds confirmed by real data: sleep kinds 0<hours<=24 (or <=16 for a single sleep-day); spo2 strictly >0 (>=50 is safe); heart rate >0. Posture per ADR-0002: quarantine the offending point rather than dropping it, so the raw record is still recoverable.
close_reason: Landed in PR #12 (merge 63ae520): the live intake now converts units instead of warning about them, applies per-kind plausibility bounds, and quarantines what it will not store. Measured on the real 3.2GB export: 50,877 -> 50,812 rows, 65 refused (0.13%), every one a confirmed artifact; all 245 legitimate zeros preserved. ADR-0007 records the decisions.

title: Verify Apple Health percent-scale (0-1 vs 0-100) on the first real export import
description:
The one unverifiable assumption left by healthie-4lf.1. Apple's percent-typed quantities (Spo2, BodyFat, GaitAsymmetry, GaitDoubleSupport) may be written to export.xml as a 0-1 fraction (0.97) or as 0-100 (97). HealthKit stores HKUnit.percent() as a fraction internally, but the EXPORTER's scaling is undocumented and no real export.xml was available during implementation, so the importer deliberately does NOT guess with a heuristic.

Mitigation already shipped: the CLI report prints, per kind, the observed value span with its unit. If spo2 comes out '0.91 .. 0.99 %' instead of '91 .. 99 %', it is visible in the first screen of output before anything downstream consumes it.

ACTION on the first real import run: read the per-kind spans in the report. If any percent kind is 0-1 scaled, add the scaling arm in healthie-shared/src/services/apple_health/units.rs and re-run — the import is idempotent, so the re-run corrects in place with no cleanup.

This matters disproportionately because healthie-4lf.2's SpO2 desaturation detection thresholds on these values; a 100x scale error there is the difference between 'no episodes' and 'every night is an episode'.
acceptance_criteria:
- First real export.xml import run, per-kind spans inspected
- Percent kinds confirmed correctly scaled, or a units.rs arm added + idempotent re-run performed
notes:
RESOLVED PENDING MERGE (2026-08-01). The verification this bead asked for happened against Steve's real 3.2GB export: all four percent-typed kinds are 0-1 FRACTIONS. The auto-flag fired on BodyFat 0.000..0.303, Spo2 0.000..0.985, GaitAsymmetry 0.000..0.900, GaitDoubleSupport 0.259..0.358.

The x100 conversion was added in response and now reads BodyFat 0.000..30.295 %, Spo2 0.000..98.500 %. The auto-flag is silent on correctly-scaled data, pinned by a test so it cannot become a false alarm.

NOT closed yet because the fix is in PR #11 (unmerged). Close alongside healthie-4lf.1 and healthie-c4x in the post-merge chore(beads) commit on main — closing now would make bd ready/bd list lie while the work is not on main.

Note for healthie-4lf.2: GaitDoubleSupport's raw 0.259..0.358 was entirely plausible AS a percentage, so a range heuristic would have fixed blood oxygen and left that one 100x low. Printing the span and waiting for real data was the right call, not merely the cautious one.
close_reason: Landed in PR #11 (merge 48fe8d6): Apple Health export.xml importer, UCUM unit conversion, and the percent-scale verification + x100 fix. Verified against the real 3.2GB/7.6M-record export: 50,877 rows, 2011-02-17..2026-07-31, 7.9s, 109MB peak.

title: ingest_hae: warn_on_unit_mismatch silently coerces units on the LIVE path
description:
Found by the plan reviewer during healthie-4lf.1 review; unrelated to that unit, filed rather than fixed inline.

healthie-shared/src/services/metrics.rs:243-247 — warn_on_unit_mismatch() emits a tracing::warn! when an HAE payload's declared units differ from MetricKind::unit(), and then stores the value ANYWAY as if it were already canonical. An HAE payload declaring units: 'kg' for Weight is stored as if it were lb — a ~2.2x error, silent apart from a log line nobody reads on an automated push with no interactive caller.

This is silent unit coercion on the live ingest path — precisely what bead healthie-4lf.1 forbids on the import path (where an unconvertible unit quarantines rather than coerces). The two paths should agree.

Options: (a) convert when a conversion is known (reuse the importer's units.rs once healthie-4lf.1 lands), (b) quarantine the point when units mismatch and no conversion exists, (c) both — convert what we can, quarantine the rest. (c) matches ADR-0002's 'never silently dropped' posture and ADR-0005 §4.

Severity: P1 because it corrupts data silently and permanently on the path that will run unattended every day once the odroid deploy (healthie-93n) lands.
acceptance_criteria:
- A units-mismatched HAE point is either converted correctly or quarantined, never stored as-is
- Live and import paths agree on unit handling
- Test covers a kg-declared Weight payload
notes:
CORRECTION 2026-08-01, verified empirically by the lead: this bead's claim that 'a NaN or infinity in an HAE payload lands unchallenged in daily_metric' is FALSE as currently wired.

serde_json (1.0.150, no arbitrary_precision) rejects non-finite at PARSE time — '1e999' and '-1e999' error with 'number out of range', bare NaN/Infinity are not valid JSON at all, and Number::from_f64 returns None for both. A serde_json::Value therefore cannot hold a non-finite float, so POST /ingest/hae returns 400 before ingest_hae is ever called.

The is_finite() guard is still worth adding, but as DEFENSE IN DEPTH rather than a live-defect fix: as_f64()'s contract is not 'finite', enabling arbitrary_precision would change the answer, and any future non-HTTP caller of ingest_hae bypasses the wire check entirely. The real invariant (the wire cannot carry it) gets pinned by its own test, so if that ever stops being true it fails loudly rather than silently promoting the guard to load-bearing.

The unit-coercion half of this bead is unaffected and remains the real P1: warn_on_unit_mismatch logs and stores anyway.

title: Project Setup & Scaffolding
Relocate bead/ADR references out of rustdoc-visible comments
description:
Enforces the CLAUDE.md rule added 2026-08-09 (commit 2f52ef5). Steve found the violation in healthie-shared/src/services/apple_health/parse.rs:429, whose doc comment opens 'healthie-55h's confirmed case'.

THE PROBLEM: /// and //! render on docs.rs, where the reader has neither the repo nor the tracker. A bare bead ID or 'ADR-0005 §4' in published docs reads as an author who does not understand their audience.

THIS IS RELOCATION, NOT DELETION. The provenance is worth keeping — it just belongs in a plain // comment, where the reader has both the repo and bd. Measured across the workspace, essentially every reference is currently in the wrong place:
  bead IDs:  10 in /// or //!,  0 in //
  ADR refs:  29 in /// or //!,  1 in //

SCOPE — the ~39 rustdoc-visible references in healthie-*/src. Files with bead IDs: services/metrics.rs (the heaviest), services/apple_health/{mod,parse,units}.rs, services/plausibility.rs, backend/src/api/{mod,ingest,health}.rs. ADR refs are spread wider.

NOT PURELY MECHANICAL: you cannot just change /// to //. The reference has to move to a // comment above the item while the remaining /// still reads well without it — and often the /// already states the substance, in which case the ID simply goes. parse.rs:429 is the model: the very next line already explains that a 0.000 SpO2 sample is a sensor artifact that put a 0.000 floor on 962 days, so the bead ID carries nothing the comment does not already say. Strike four words and it is better AND public-safe.

FORWARD REFERENCES need rewording rather than relocation: 'see healthie-1ru' and 'deferred to healthie-4lf.2' should describe the future work, not name its ticket — 'until a provenance column exists' rather than 'see healthie-1ru'.

ADR MARKDOWN (docs/adr/*.md, 56 bead refs) is a separate question, deliberately not in this bead's scope: ADRs ship together so ADR-to-ADR references are fine, but bead IDs there are dangling unless .beads/ ships too. That decision belongs with healthie-ddz.
acceptance_criteria:
- No bead ID, ADR-NNNN, or PR number appears in any /// or //! in healthie-*/src
- Every relocated reference lands in a // comment, or its substance is stated inline and the ID dropped
- The remaining doc comments read correctly standalone — check with cargo doc --no-deps and read a few
- just ci green
notes: Run AFTER PR #12 merges — it touches several of the same files (metrics.rs, plausibility.rs, units.rs, apple_health/*) and would conflict. Small and mechanical enough to fold into another unit rather than run alone. Related: healthie-ddz (pre-public pass) covers the ADR-markdown half and the name removal.

title: Pre-public pass: remove the owner's name from the repo surface
description:
Steve's call 2026-08-03: the repo may go public. The name is not severe PII and can stay in git history and commit authorship — the goal is removing it from the SURFACE (source, docs, generated exports), not rewriting history.

ADR-0007 is already done (commit 41c0c53, PR #12): 'the first real import', 'the HAE MCP server', 'the real 3.2 GB export'. This bead covers everything else.

SCOPE — 46 occurrences across 13 remaining tracked files, plus committed beads:

A. LLM-FACING TEXT (needs a decision, not a sed) — 15 occurrences:
   healthie-mcp/src/handler.rs (5), healthie-mcp/src/schemas.rs (10)
   These are MCP tool descriptions and schema doc comments that an LLM READS AT RUNTIME, e.g.
     'Persist a batch of intake claims — what Steve CLAIMS, with honest confidence'
     'READ THE CLAIMS BACK to Steve before calling'
     'subject: self = about Steve; father etc. = a relative'
     'healthie MCP: the system of record for Steve health — concerns, goals...'
   Replacing the name changes the conversational surface. Pick a replacement noun deliberately and apply it consistently: 'the user', 'you' (addressing the subject), or restructure to avoid a referent. ADR-0002 fixes the system as single-user ('Steve only, full model'), so 'the user' is unambiguous. Verify the MCP integration tests still assert sensible text afterward.

B. INTERNAL DOC COMMENTS (straight substitution) — 13 occurrences:
   healthie-shared/src/entities/claim.rs (3), inputs/claim.rs (2), services/claim.rs (3),
   services/apple_health/accumulate.rs (3), services/plausibility.rs (2),
   services/units.rs (2), healthie-backend/src/apple_health.rs (1),
   healthie-mcp/tests/mcp_integration_test.rs (2)
   Mostly 'Steve's real 15-year import', 'what Steve claims about his health'. Use 'the user's' / 'the real import'.

C. ADRs (immutable once Accepted — annotate, do not edit history of decisions):
   docs/adr/0002 (1), 0004 (8), 0006 (1)
   ADR-0004 is the heavy one. These are Accepted documents; CLAUDE.md says supersede rather than edit. BUT a name is not a decision, so a de-identification pass is arguably a non-substantive edit. Decide the policy explicitly and record it — do not quietly rewrite an Accepted ADR without saying so.

D. COMMITTED BEADS — 84 occurrences:
   .beads/issues.jsonl (80), .beads/README.md (4)
   issues.jsonl is a GENERATED export — editing the file alone accomplishes nothing, the next 'bd export' re-emits it. The name must come out of the bead descriptions themselves via 'bd update <id> --description=...', then re-export. Many were written during the 2026-08-01/02 sessions ('Steve's real export', 'Steve's north-star ask').

EXPLICITLY OUT OF SCOPE (Steve's call): git history, and commit authorship (every commit is 'Steve Loveless <steve.loveless@gmail.com>'). Also unchanged: the remote is github.com/turboladen/healthie.

SEPARATE DECISION WORTH MAKING AT THE SAME TIME: .beads/issues.jsonl also carries health specifics — a 49.88h sleep night, a 0.000 SpO2 floor across 962 days, body-fat and weight ranges, the breathing-interruption history motivating healthie-4lf.2. That is arguably more identifying than a first name, and it is in a file that regenerates from the Dolt DB. Decide whether it goes public, gets genericized, or whether .beads/ is excluded from the public repo entirely.

- LLM-facing text in handler.rs/schemas.rs uses one consistent replacement noun; MCP integration tests still pass and still assert sensible text

title: HAE blood_pressure is never exploded — every push quarantines it
description:
Found by the plan reviewer during healthie-ei8/55h/c47 review (2026-08-01).

ADR-0006 §2 named this as 'the natural follow-up' and no bead was filed for it.

HAE models blood pressure as a SINGLE 'blood_pressure' metric carrying systolic and diastolic FIELDS per data point — the same 1-to-many shape as sleep_analysis. map_hae_name has no arm for it, so it falls through to HaeMapping::Unknown and quarantines on every push that carries it.

Meanwhile PR #11 added BloodPressureSystolic and BloodPressureDiastolic as MetricKind variants, reachable ONLY from the Apple Health import path. So the kinds exist, the import populates them, and the live path cannot.

Fix: give map_hae_name a Sleep-like 1-to-many arm for blood_pressure, exploding each point's systolic/diastolic fields into the two existing kinds — mirroring sleep_rows(). Note HK_METRICS deliberately records None as the HAE counterpart for both kinds (ADR-0006 §1: 'no HAE NAME resolves to either'), which stays true — the explosion is name-to-many-kinds, not name-to-name. The agreement test asserts that absence positively, so check it still expresses the right thing after this lands.
acceptance_criteria:
- An HAE payload carrying blood_pressure lands BloodPressureSystolic and BloodPressureDiastolic rows
- It no longer appears in the quarantine report
- The HK_METRICS None-counterpart assertion still expresses a true statement

title: import: stale-row detection misses kinds a re-map stops producing entirely
description:
Found by /code-review xhigh on healthie-4lf.1 (2026-08-01), skipped as a policy change rather than fixed.

find_stale_rows (healthie-shared/src/services/apple_health/mod.rs) scopes its query to kinds the run PRODUCED. So a mapping fix that stops producing a kind entirely leaves every one of that kind's rows unreported and beyond --replace-range's reach — which is exactly the re-mapping scenario the mechanism advertises.

Concrete: correct a bad mapping so HKQuantityTypeIdentifierWalkingSpeed lands on StepLength instead of WalkingSpeed. Re-run. The per-kind ranges map has no WalkingSpeed entry, so its decade of now-known-wrong rows is never queried, never listed in stale_rows, and cannot be deleted.

WHY IT WAS NOT JUST FIXED: widening the query to every kind present in the date range is not obviously correct. A kind absent from this export is equally consistent with 'no longer mapped' (stale, should go) and 'this export does not cover it' (fine, must stay) — e.g. a metric from a device Steve stopped wearing, or one HAE pushes but Apple's export omits. That is the same undecidability as the provenance problem in healthie-1ru, and getting it wrong means --replace-range deletes good data.

Options: (a) require the operator to name kinds explicitly (--replace-kinds), (b) report-only for unproduced kinds with no delete offered, (c) wait for provenance (healthie-1ru) which makes it decidable for rows written after that lands.

ADR-0006 now states this limit explicitly rather than implying coverage.
acceptance_criteria:
- A re-map that abandons a kind either reports its rows or the docs state plainly that it does not
- Whatever is chosen cannot delete rows that are merely uncovered by this export

title: Import Apple Health symptom/event categories into observations (not daily_metric)
description:

  HKCategoryTypeIdentifierSleepApneaEvent                          1 record
  HKCategoryTypeIdentifierShortnessOfBreath                        2
  HKCategoryTypeIdentifierRapidPoundingOrFlutteringHeartbeat      16
  HKCategoryTypeIdentifierSkippedHeartbeat                        14
  HKCategoryTypeIdentifierDizziness                                4
  HKCategoryTypeIdentifierFatigue                                  6

WHY NOT daily_metric: these are timestamped EVENTS carrying a severity (HKCategoryValueSeverity{NotPresent,Mild,Moderate,Severe}), not daily numeric aggregates. Forcing 'dizziness = 2.0 on 2024-03-11' into (kind, date, value) is lossy and semantically wrong.

WHERE THEY BELONG: the existing observations table already models exactly this — occurred_at (DateTimeUtc), kind (Note|Symptom), body (String), severity (Option<i32>), concern_id, reviewed. ADR-0002 already lists log_symptom as an MCP verb. These are symptoms.

TWO BLOCKERS that make this a real unit rather than a mapping-table addition:
1. NO UNIQUE INDEX on observations. daily_metric has UNIQUE(kind,date), which is what makes the importer idempotent; observations has nothing (verified in m20260716_000001_initial_schema.rs). Re-running the import would DUPLICATE every symptom row, breaking the importer's central contract. Needs a migration adding a dedup key — likely UNIQUE(origin, kind, body, occurred_at) — plus an upsert path.
2. ObservationOrigin has only SelfReported | Ai | Rules. These arrive from a device (SleepApneaEvent is watch-detected; the symptom logs are user-tapped but via Apple Health, not via healthie). Needs a new variant — likely Device or AppleHealth. Text column with no CHECK constraint, so no migration needed for the enum itself, but the wire contract and any exhaustive matches must be updated.

ALSO decide: severity mapping (HKCategoryValueSeverity* -> i32, and what NotPresent means — probably skip the row entirely rather than store a zero), and whether SleepApneaEvent is a symptom observation or belongs with healthie-4lf.2's Episode entity given it is device-detected rather than self-reported.
acceptance_criteria:
- The six category types import into observations with correct occurred_at, severity, and body
- Re-running the import does NOT duplicate rows (unique index + upsert, proven by test)
- ObservationOrigin gains a device/apple-health variant; exhaustive matches updated
- NotPresent severity handled deliberately (skipped, not stored as zero)
- Promoted names no longer appear in the import's quarantine report

title: import-apple-health: make --replace-range deletion recoverable
description:
Raised by the round-2 reviewer on healthie-4lf.1 (2026-07-31) as the design that would retire an objection rather than document around it.

--replace-range deletes daily_metric rows inside the imported range that a re-run did not rewrite. Its blast radius is verified-bounded (only kinds this run produced, inside each kind's own produced date range, minus exactly what it wrote, in one transaction, off by default) and the CLI warning honestly refuses to assert whether a given stale row came from an earlier bad import or from a live HAE push on a day the export does not cover — because daily_metric has no provenance and NOTHING records which.

That honesty is the right posture for an undecidable question, but the better answer is to make the operation recoverable: dump the rows to a file (or a side table) before deleting them, so a wrong call is undoable. That removes the need for the operator to adjudicate an undecidable question correctly on the first try.

Note per healthie-1ru: adding a provenance column does NOT solve this for pre-existing rows, since it can only label rows written after it lands.
acceptance_criteria:
- Rows removed by --replace-range are dumped somewhere recoverable before deletion
- The dump location is named in the CLI output
- Restoring from the dump is documented

title: import-apple-health: --dry-run to inspect the report before writing
description:
Raised by the final code reviewer on healthie-4lf.1 (2026-07-31).

The percent-scale tripwire (healthie-4u7) is the CLI report's per-kind observed value span — but the report is rendered only AFTER txn.commit(). So the operator learns that Spo2 came out 0.91..0.99 instead of 91..99 only once a decade of mis-scaled history is already written.

It is recoverable (the import is idempotent for value-only fixes, and the fix is one arm in apple_health/units.rs), but a --dry-run that parses, aggregates, and renders the full report WITHOUT persisting would let the operator check the spans before writing anything. Cheap: the architecture already splits parse_export_xml (sync, DB-free) from persist_import (async, DB-only), so a dry run is 'call the first, render, skip the second'.

Worth pairing with the auto-flag for percent-unit kinds (a value_max <= 1.0 on a %-unit kind is decisive evidence of fraction scaling).
acceptance_criteria:
- --dry-run renders the identical report without any DB write
- Documented in the CLI help alongside the idempotency caveat

title: quarantined_metric: add an ingest-path discriminator column
description:
Found by the plan reviewer during healthie-4lf.1 review.

Today quarantined_metric holds only HAE-vocabulary raw_names (e.g. 'brand_new_metric'). Once the Apple Health importer (healthie-4lf.1) lands, the same table also holds HK-vocabulary names (e.g. 'HKQuantityTypeIdentifierDietaryWater') — two vocabularies in one table, distinguishable only by string prefix.

They also arrive at different granularities: the live path writes one row per (raw_name, date); the importer writes one row per raw_name total, with the count in raw_point._import.records_seen (healthie-4lf.1 D5, which narrows ADR-0005 §4 for that path only — recorded in ADR-0006).

Add a source_path / origin discriminator column (values: hae, apple-export) so a reader can tell the two apart without prefix-sniffing, and so promoting a quarantined name knows which mapping table to add it to.

Ideally lands BEFORE the first real import run (healthie-sj9), since it is a migration over a table that will by then hold real rows.
notes: Third item for this bead (hardening-author, 2026-08-02): with one quarantine row per (raw_name, date), two equally-total losses on the same key are order-dependent — the second overwrites the first and one reading is unrecoverable whatever the tie-break. The live path now prefers a total loss over a partial one when choosing which point to preserve, which handles the common case, but two totals cannot both be kept under the current schema. A discriminator column does not fix this by itself; it needs the key widened or a per-point row.

title: M2: Apple Health anomaly windows → episode candidates (needs Episode entity + ADR)
description:
Second half of healthie-4lf, deliberately split out of the importer (healthie-4lf.1).

Steve's north-star ask: a past Claude pass over his full Apple Health export surfaced spells of low oxygen / breathing interruptions he had NOT noticed himself. Reproducing that durably means detecting anomaly windows over the backfilled history and surfacing them as episode / intake-question candidates.

Why it is NOT in the importer PR:
1. There is no Episode entity in the schema — grep finds 'episode' only in ADR-0002 prose. Inventing one (raw high-resolution series for flagged windows, per ADR-0002 'Data depth') is an ADR-level decision, not something to bury inside an importer.
2. Detection is far easier to design against real data already sitting in daily_metric than against fixtures.

Scope when picked up:
- Superseding/extending ADR for the Episode entity + raw-series retention for flagged windows
- Detectors: SpO2 desaturation spells, HRV dips, breathing-disturbance spikes (thresholds on daily_metric.max — the AvgMinMax policy in 4lf.1 preserves the worst-of-day figure precisely for this)
- Surface candidates into the M1c intake question flow so the real baseline (healthie-sj9) is data-first
notes:
CRITICAL constraint inherited from healthie-4lf.1 (2026-07-31), flagged because ADR-0006 §3 is easy to miss:

Sum-kind daily_metric values (Steps, ActiveEnergy, ExerciseMinutes, StandMinutes, WalkingDistance) are a LOWER BOUND, not a measurement. export.xml carries the same interval from multiple devices (iPhone + Watch), so the importer stores the maximum single-source total rather than the sum — naive summation would roughly DOUBLE a day. Where two devices each captured a disjoint half-day, the stored value is one half. Anomaly detection written as if these were measurements will produce false 'activity dropped' signals on multi-device days. The CLI report prints per-Sum-kind the count of days with >1 contributing source and the sum-vs-max ratio, so the magnitude is knowable.

Second inherited constraint: SleepTotal can be LESS than the sum of its stages once multi-source segments overlap (union of asleep <= sum of per-stage unions). Correct behavior, but it breaks the invariant a naive reader assumes.

Third: threshold on daily_metric.max, not value, for the desaturation/breathing work — the AvgMinMax policy exists precisely so max preserves the worst reading of the day while value keeps the typical-day baseline needed to judge whether it is unusual.

Fourth: healthie-4u7 (percent scale, 0-1 vs 0-100) MUST be settled before thresholds are chosen. A 100x scale error is the difference between 'no episodes' and 'every night is an episode'.

title: M2: Apple Health export.xml importer — streaming parse → daily_metric
description:
First half of healthie-4lf. One-time backfill of Apple Health history into the curated daily_metric store, so the real baseline intake (healthie-sj9) and M2b's reading layer (healthie-bx9) start from years of data instead of a blank DB.

Scope:
- Streaming XML parse of export.xml (quick-xml Reader, NOT a DOM parse — the file is routinely multi-GB).
- HKQuantityTypeIdentifier* / HKCategoryTypeIdentifier* name mapping reusing ADR-0005 §4's curated/excluded/quarantined trichotomy. Curated names must land on the SAME MetricKind as their HAE counterpart in map_hae_name.
- Per-kind daily aggregation (DailyAgg: Sum / AvgMinMax / Mean / Max) — export.xml is per-reading, HAE is pre-aggregated, so the importer must reconstruct the daily rollup. Policy decided by Steve 2026-07-31, see the DESIGN field, which is authoritative.
  NOTE: an earlier revision of this description listed a fifth 'Last' variant. It is VESTIGIAL — it predates Steve's policy decision, which maps nothing to Last. Four variants ship; a fifth unconstructed variant would fail clippy -D warnings via dead_code. Caught at the plan-review gate 2026-07-31.
- Sleep: HKCategoryTypeIdentifierSleepAnalysis records are timed segments (startDate..endDate per stage); fold segment durations per stage per night into the existing SleepTotal/Deep/Rem/Core/Awake/TimeInBed kinds, coalescing overlapping segments (two sources recording one night must not double it).
- Unit conversion to MetricKind::unit() canonical units (export.xml carries per-record unit attrs: kg vs lb, etc). A unit that cannot be converted must not be silently coerced.
- Local calendar day from the record's own offset, never UTC-converted (ADR-0005 §5).
- Batched idempotent upsert, last-write-wins on (kind, date) — same contract as ingest_hae — reporting per-kind diffs against any pre-existing rows BEFORE overwriting them.
- CLI: healthie-backend import-apple-health <path>, reporting counts/date-range/quarantined names.

Out of scope (see sibling bead healthie-4lf.2): anomaly windows / episode candidates.
design:
Aggregation policy (Steve, 2026-07-31): standing preference is KEEP THE SPREAD, discard nothing — min/max already exist on the row so preserving the day's range is free.
- Sum: Steps, ActiveEnergy, ExerciseMinutes, StandMinutes, WalkingDistance
- AvgMinMax: HeartRate, Spo2, RespiratoryRate, Hrv, Weight, BodyFat, CardioRecovery, BreathingDisturbances
- Mean: WalkingSpeed, GaitAsymmetry, GaitDoubleSupport, StepLength, RestingHeartRate
- Max: Vo2Max — deliberately chosen knowing it ratchets upward and will NOT surface a genuine decline; Apple's per-workout estimate is noisy enough that the daily best is the more trustworthy figure. Revisit here first if declines must surface.
- Sleep stages never hit daily_agg() — separate segment-duration path; the exhaustive match makes a new MetricKind fail to compile until its policy is decided.
Rationale per kind: Weight AvgMinMax over Last so a stray evening weigh-in cannot become the day's official weight; BreathingDisturbances AvgMinMax so max holds the worst night (episode detection thresholds on it) while value keeps the typical-night baseline.
Business logic lives in healthie-shared (ADR-0002); the backend owns only the CLI subcommand.
acceptance_criteria:
- Fixture-driven tests parse a hand-authored export.xml covering scalar, aggregate, sleep-segment, unknown-name, non-canonical-unit, and multi-reading-per-day cases
- Curated export.xml names land on the same MetricKind as their HAE counterparts (a test asserts the two mappings agree)
- Unknown record types quarantine verbatim, never drop
- Re-running the import is idempotent (no duplicate rows)
- Multi-GB file imports without loading the document into memory
- just ci passes (fmt-check, build, test, clippy pedantic -D warnings)

title: daily_metric units: adopt uom (+ UCUM canonical) if/when conversions or clinical export arrive
description: MetricKind::unit() returns &'static str, used ONLY by warn_on_unit_mismatch (display/sanity, logged) — never stored, computed, or converted. Fine while display-only. Revisit WHEN either (a) unit conversions become real (metric/imperial display or normalization — time/distance likely), or (b) clinical export lands (M4 summarize_for_appointment → FHIR/HL7, which use UCUM). Then replace &str with the uom crate (compile-time dimensional analysis + conversions) and consider UCUM as the canonical vocabulary. NOTE: HAE emits its own unit strings (count/min, ml/(kg·min), lb, mi, %, ms, hr), NOT UCUM — so this also implies a HAE→canonical unit mapping. No conversion/export consumer exists today. Steve's call 2026-07-31: skip until needed, maybe never.
notes:
TRIGGER CONDITION MET 2026-08-01. This bead said 'revisit WHEN unit conversions become real' — they now are. healthie-4lf.1's apple_health/units.rs hand-codes ~20 conversion constants (kg/g/st/oz->lb, km/m/ft/yd->mi, kJ/J->kcal, km-per-hr and m/s->mi/hr, cm/mm/m/ft->in, s/hr->min, min/s->hr). Steve's call: do not reinvent this wheel — bring in a library.

Scope note for whoever does it: a units library replaces the NUMERIC CONSTANTS only. It does NOT replace (a) the string-normalization layer that maps Apple's and HAE's vocabularies onto canonical spellings ('mL/min·kg', 'lbs', 'mph', 'kph'), which is vocabulary mapping rather than dimensional analysis; (b) the dimensionless kinds (%, count, count/min, ms); (c) the percent x100 fraction-to-percent scaling, which is a scale convention, not a unit conversion. The constants are the valuable part to outsource — a wrong digit there is silent and permanent.

Being done now rather than deferred because the hand-rolled constants are currently in PR #11; shipping them and swapping later would mean reasoning about whether stored values changed meaning.

title: Declare strum directly instead of reaching through sea_orm::strum
description:
Nine files do 'use sea_orm::strum::IntoEnumIterator' — baseline_intake.rs, quarantined_metric.rs (x2), accumulate.rs, mapping.rs, claim.rs (services), metrics.rs, plausibility.rs, units.rs. That is a latent coupling: it depends on sea-orm continuing to re-export strum, at a version compatible with how we use it. Declaring strum directly in [workspace.dependencies] and importing 'strum::IntoEnumIterator' removes the reach-through. Zero behavior change.

VERSION TRAP — do not pin the latest. Cargo.lock currently has strum 0.26.3 (pulled by sea-orm 1.1) and NO strum_macros: sea-orm does not enable strum's 'derive' feature, it emits EnumIter impls from its own sea-orm-macros. Latest strum is 0.28.0.

Declaring strum = "0.28" puts TWO strum crates in the tree. EnumIter (from sea-orm-macros) implements 0.26's IntoEnumIterator; a 0.28 import is a DIFFERENT trait. The symptom is a confusing 'trait not implemented' error on a type that visibly has .iter().

So pin strum = "0.26" to match sea-orm. Note this is a deliberate exception to ADR-0002's 'pin the latest stable of everything' policy — record why in the Cargo.toml comment, since the next person to run a dependency sweep will otherwise 'fix' it. It also means strum upgrades are coupled to sea-orm's; revisit when sea-orm ships a strum-0.28-compatible release.
design:
EXPLICITLY NOT DOING: replacing QuarantineReason::as_str / parse (entities/quarantined_metric.rs) with strum's AsRefStr / EnumString derives. Steve raised this 2026-08-09 and the survey says no, for now:

1. It is the ONLY hand-rolled enum-to-string impl in the workspace. Every other closed vocabulary (14+) is a DeriveActiveEnum where SeaORM generates the DB conversion from string_value. QuarantineReason is hand-rolled precisely because it is NOT a DB column — it lives inside raw_point JSON. So strum would replace ~20 lines in exactly one place.

2. as_str's exhaustive match is a COMPILE-TIME guarantee that strum removes. Today, adding a variant fails to compile until its spelling is decided. With #[strum(serialize_all = "kebab-case")] a new variant always compiles and silently derives a string. Worse, RENAMING a variant would silently change the persisted spelling and orphan every existing _import.reason row. Those six literals are not duplication — they are a wire contract with stored data.

3. This is the 'enforced by shape, not by a check' principle (ADR-0005's closing line), and parse's own doc comment already makes the argument.

REVISIT WHEN: sea-orm ships a strum-0.28-compatible release (removing the pin conflict), OR a second non-DB string vocabulary appears — at two, the duplication argument starts to outweigh the exhaustiveness one.
acceptance_criteria:
- strum declared in [workspace.dependencies] at the version sea-orm uses, with a comment explaining the deliberate non-latest pin
- All nine sea_orm::strum:: reach-throughs replaced with direct strum:: imports
- just ci green; no behavior change
- QuarantineReason::as_str and parse left as they are
notes: Small enough to fold into whatever unit runs next rather than standing alone. Raised by Steve 2026-08-09 while reviewing QuarantineReason.

title: Remove already-stored artifact rows from imported stores (65 rows)
description:
Deferred deliberately during healthie-55h (2026-08-02), now with an exact count.

The plausibility bounds only affect NEW writes. Any store already populated by an import before the bounds landed holds the artifacts they now refuse — measured at exactly 65 rows on Steve's real 3.2GB export: body-fat 40, spo2 23, sleep-total 1, time-in-bed 2 (that last being the 2023-12-29 Sleep Cycle stuck-recording day).

On the IMPORT path these self-heal: a re-import no longer produces those (kind, date) keys, so they surface as stale_rows and --replace-range removes them. ADR-0007 records honestly that the LIVE path has no equivalent sweep at all.

Not urgent while no production store exists (the odroid deploy, healthie-93n, has not happened and healthie-sj9 specifies a fresh DB). Becomes relevant only if a store predating this change is ever carried forward.

title: Live path has no sweep for quarantine rows whose name later becomes excluded
description:
Found by hardening-author during healthie-ei8/55h/c47 (2026-08-02), noted not fixed.

The import path has clear_promoted_quarantine, which retires a quarantine row once its name becomes curated-or-excluded. The live path now retires a row when the same (hae_name, date) later writes cleanly — but there is no equivalent for a name moved from Unknown into EXCLUDED_HAE_NAMES. Such a name never produces a successful write, so its old quarantine rows have nothing to sweep them.

Nuisance only — no data impact, and the rows are a bounded one-per-name-per-day from before the exclusion. Note the live-path hardening strictly improved the surrounding situation: before it, NO live quarantine complaint was ever retired.

Natural sibling of healthie-1ru; the discriminator column would make a live-path sweep straightforward to scope safely.

title: import: quarantine rows with unit reasons can never be cleared
description:
Found by /code-review xhigh on healthie-4lf.1 (2026-08-01), skipped as needing a rule rather than a patch.

A quarantine row written with reason missing-unit or unconvertible-unit has no path to removal:
- clear_promoted_quarantine skips it, because that sweep is deliberately scoped to NAME-based reasons only (a name quarantined over a bad unit has not been 'promoted', and sweeping it would be wrong — this scoping was itself a fix from an earlier review round).
- drop_other_dates only runs for names quarantined in the CURRENT run, and once the unit is fixed the name is no longer quarantined at all.

So: quarantine HKQuantityTypeIdentifierBodyMass for unit='furlong', later add furlong to to_ucum, re-run. The records now import correctly and the row survives forever, advertising a problem that no longer exists. That is precisely the class of staleness clear_promoted_quarantine was written to eliminate.

Needs a rule, which is why it was not just patched: 'delete unit-reason rows for names that imported cleanly this run' is probably right, but it has to not fire when the name legitimately produced no rows this run (a date range the export does not cover), and it interacts with healthie-1ru's one-row-per-name-vs-per-date question.

Low severity — a stale quarantine row misleads a reader but corrupts no metric.
acceptance_criteria:
- Fixing a unit and re-running leaves no quarantine row for that name
- The rule cannot delete a quarantine row for a name that is still genuinely unconvertible

title: upsert_metric nulls min/max/source on the UPDATE path
description:
Found by the plan reviewer during healthie-4lf.1 review; filed rather than fixed inline.

healthie-shared/src/services/metrics.rs:271-274 — the UPDATE branch of upsert_metric unconditionally Sets min, max, and source. So a later HAE push carrying a scalar qty for a kind that previously landed an aggregate (Avg/Min/Max) silently NULLs the existing min/max.

Defensible as last-write-wins, but ADR-0005 §5 describes the ROW upserting, not columns being nulled, and the behavior is untested either way. Decide explicitly whether a scalar re-push should clear a prior aggregate's spread, then encode that decision in a test. Matters more once healthie-4lf.1's backfill and the live path both write the same (kind, date) rows.
acceptance_criteria:
- Explicit decision recorded (preserve vs null) with a test asserting it
- ADR-0005 §5 clarified if the behavior differs from what it implies
close_reason: Landed in PR #12 (merge 63ae520): the live intake now converts units instead of warning about them, applies per-kind plausibility bounds, and quarantines what it will not store. Measured on the real 3.2GB export: 50,877 -> 50,812 rows, 65 refused (0.13%), every one a confirmed artifact; all 245 legitimate zeros preserved. ADR-0007 records the decisions.

title: Convert ALL migrations from Alias::new strings to DeriveIden enums (type-safe, DRY)
description: All 5 migrations (initial_schema, mcp_token, claims, daily_metric, auth_token) use Alias::new("...") string literals for table/column identifiers, repeating each name across the column def AND its index — a typo mismatch compiles but fails at runtime (only partly caught by round-trip tests). Convert every migration to #[derive(DeriveIden)] enum identifiers (define each name once, reference in both the column def and the index) — type-safe and DRY. App is PRE-PRODUCTION (never deployed or run), so rewriting migration bodies in place is safe (no deployed DB depends on the exact DDL, no migration-immutability concern). Do this BEFORE the migration count grows (each new Alias-style migration is more to convert). Include updating the CLAUDE.md migration-style note to mandate DeriveIden going forward so the good convention propagates, not the Alias smell. Steve's call 2026-07-31: fix ALL of them to establish good, succinct conventions.

title: daily_metric: MetricValue domain enum (Scalar/Aggregate) over the flat value/min/max columns
description: The daily_metric entity Model IS the DB row; flat scalar columns (value f64, min/max Option<f64>) are correct for per-column queryability (M2b trends, M3 rules do SELECT value / AVG(value) — an enum can't be a single column without collapsing to JSON and killing that). But the mutually-exclusive Options are a weak invariant: a row with min set + max null, or min/max on a scalar metric, is representable. Add a DOMAIN-layer enum MetricValue { Scalar(f64), Aggregate { avg: f64, min: f64, max: f64 } } (a type above the row, same pattern as inputs::* vs entity Models), with Model::reading() -> MetricValue and the ingest service constructing rows THROUGH it, so the both-or-neither invariant is enforced at one boundary and readers match on a shape instead of 3 loose columns. Land WITH its first consumer, summarize_trends (M2b, healthie-bx9) — no reader of the value shape exists in M2, so adding it now would be an unused abstraction. Steve's call 2026-07-31: do it, deferred to M2b.

title: ingest_hae: bulk on_conflict upsert for large backfill payloads
description: metrics::ingest_hae does one SELECT + one INSERT/UPDATE per data point (N DB round-trips per payload). Fine for daily HAE pushes (small), but the Apple Health history backfill (healthie-4lf) sends large payloads where a single bulk INSERT ... ON CONFLICT(kind,date) DO UPDATE would collapse to one statement per metric. Deferred from M2 U2 (the explicit insert/update branch is the plan-mandated never-.save()-with-Set-PK pattern and preserves last-write-wins clarity; ON CONFLICT is a design change). Surfaced by the U2 code-review. Do when picking up healthie-4lf.
